notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide and docs/evidence/messagefield.md at cba512f. The guide's Sources note was checked on 8 October 2026 on the 5 October build, which the evidence's 636f3f5 check names (mirror v0.1.78-636f3f5, Biscuit's main at 636f3f5), so items citing it carry that build. The evidence's first check (2 October, 0.1.78-3795b4c) is out of date where its 636f3f5 section says #187 is fixed: typed text no longer looks like a placeholder when idle, the field now has errorMessage and supportText, aria-invalid and aria-required are set, and a disabled field leaves the tab order; the Storybook MDX line that there is no errorMessage or support-text API is out of date too. None of those sentences is used. The 2 October lines used here (the state cascade, maxLength stopping typing, showCounter without a limit, the rows height, and the MDX's label and placeholder advice) still hold on the installed source. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). GitHub shows MessageField.tsx, the token file and typography.ts byte-identical at v0.1.78-636f3f5 and v0.1.78-dbe0e02; of what the field uses, only SupportText changed (long text may shrink and wrap). Installed MessageField.tsx matches every guide sentence used here, read from source, not run: the wrapper and text area are 100% wide; the text area is the 108 px token tall, or rows × 21 plus 2 × 12 px padding when rows is set, with a multiline input and overflow hidden; the wrapper gap is 8 px; the counter shows count/maxLength when maxLength is set and showCounter isn't false, and maxLength goes to the input, so typing stops at the limit; isRequired adds “ *” after the label in the Negative token; the state is derived (invalid, disabled, read only, focus, idle) and overrides FormField States in modes; typed text keeps the Active (dark) colour unless disabled, while the placeholder uses Idle; isReadOnly and isDisabled make the input not editable, and isDisabled also turns off pointer events and, on the web, sets aria-disabled and tabIndex -1; on the web aria-invalid, aria-required and aria-describedby (pointing at the line under the text area) are set; the accessible name is accessibilityLabel, then label, then placeholder; errorMessage replaces supportText while invalid, in the Error status. The tokens give a white fill in every state, a purple Active border, a red Error label and border, a grey Read Only label and border, and grey Disabled text and border. No guide sentence is contradicted. Two guide sentences describe only the default: “a counter that shows only with a limit” (Sources) and “Without a limit there is no counter” (Configuration); showCounter shows a bare count without a limit (evidence fact). Sizing's “The counter sits 8 px below” holds for a field with no message; with support text or an error, the message sits between the text area and the counter (evidence fact on errorMessage). Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every MessageField, Card, VStack, Button, Text and FormField) and no other modes. They use the guide's own copy. The In context example repeats the guide's composition (a Card holding a VStack with the field and a Submit Button) with the screen's state reduced to an empty message and no error. Left out of examples: the thanks Text the screen shows after a valid submit (screen state), the guide's Host and Surface wrapper (docs-only), the playground (Label, Limit, Rows, State and Required controls and the Characters readout), the Read only, Disabled, With a limit, No limit and Content cards (an entry carries at most three examples), and the Don'ts. Not recorded: name and Form validation errors (the evidence brief's Limits keep them out of the guide), defaultValue, autoFocus, accessibilityHint, testID, onFocus and onBlur, which the guide doesn't cover; style, textareaStyle and inputStyle, which the building rules keep off Coin components; the evidence's measured Light colours; dark mode, per the pack's rules. The label and placeholder content rule rests on the Storybook MDX as the evidence records it (2 October), not on the guide. Content bad is empty: the Don'ts show configurations (a hidden counter, an error with no message, a short value in a four-line box), not bad wording, so they are recorded as configuration rules and avoidWhen. Gaps hold only the Figma differences the Sources note states; #187 is fixed and verified on 636f3f5, so it is not a gap.

examples.purpose: Report a problem, the guide's In context: a Card holds a required field with a 500-character limit and a Submit Button. The screen owns the text (value and onChangeText); when people tap Submit it checks the message and sets isInvalid, and errorMessage says what to fix. The button stays enabled.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <VStack>
    <MessageField
      label="Describe your issue"
      placeholder="What happened, and when?"
      maxLength={500}
      isRequired
      value=""
      onChangeText={() => {}}
      isInvalid={false}
      errorMessage="Add a few more details, at least 20 characters"
    />
    <Button label="Submit" onPress={() => {}} />
  </VStack>
</Card>

evidenceFacts.name: FormField States
evidenceFacts.description: MessageField sets this mode itself from its props and focus: invalid gives Error, then disabled gives Disabled, read-only gives Read Only, focus gives Active, otherwise Idle. A value passed in modes is ignored.
evidenceFacts.quote: State cascade: invalid → Error; disabled → Disabled; read-only → Read Only; focused → Active; otherwise Idle. `modes['FormField States']` is ignored.

evidenceFacts.name: errorMessage
evidenceFacts.description: Replaces supportText only while the field is invalid; the message sits between the text area and the counter.
evidenceFacts.quote: `errorMessage` replaces `supportText` only while the field is invalid (as in FormField). The message sits between the text area and the counter.

evidenceFacts.name: maxLength
evidenceFacts.description: Typing stops at the limit, and the counter then reads the limit out of the limit (200/200 for 200).

evidenceFacts.name: showCounter
evidenceFacts.description: With showCounter and no maxLength, the counter shows a bare count.

evidenceFacts.name: rows
evidenceFacts.description: The text area is rows × 21 + 24 px tall when rows is set, otherwise the 108 px token (four rows); text scrolls inside it.
evidenceFacts.quote: Height: `rows × 21 + 24` when `rows` is set; otherwise the 108 px token (four rows). Text scrolls inside the box.

evidenceFacts.name: isDisabled
evidenceFacts.description: On the web a disabled field has aria-disabled and tabindex -1, so Tab skips it.

evidenceFacts.name: isRequired
evidenceFacts.description: On the web the text area has aria-required, and the asterisk uses the Negative (red) token.
evidenceFacts.quote: `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` are set, and the asterisk uses the Negative token.

gaps.text: Figma's Message Field has a fixed “0/140” counter and its states are variable modes; the package adds the required mark, a rows option, a counter that shows only with a limit, and support text or an error message below the text area, none of which Figma has.

from.quote: Figma’s Message Field is a 328 × 159 component with a label, a 108 px text area, and a fixed “0/140” counter; its states are variable modes. The package adds the required mark, a rows option, a counter that shows only with a limit, and support text or an error message below the text area.
